label: late-sequence / <DEL> steps when the first token is a,y,d,0,c,q,s
explanation: Fires only from t=4 to t=9 at the end of the original phase and on the <DEL> step (about 65% of mass is at <DEL>), never during the copy phase, and almost never at t<5 or for L<=4. It depends strongly on which token came first: rate and mass concentrate when first_tok is in {a,y,d,0,c,q,s} (about 4x lift each; b,u,v are weak). On original-phase steps it prefers inputs o and z (and to a lesser extent 2,3) that appear for the first time. Longer sequences (L>=6) fire more often. Activation magnitude is larger at <DEL> and with the favoured first tokens (higher quartiles are better covered). The predicate is imprecise (dev P=0.43, R=0.63, mass 0.74): many <DEL> steps with a favoured first token stay silent, which suggests a dependence on the rest of the stored sequence that this predicate does not capture.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: a, d, 0, y, c, q; least: p, k, j, l) and the next token to output (most: a, 0, y, s, c, q; least: p, r, 3, o); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, t=5, t=7.
